buttonLabel: "Explore cultural journeys through four countries"
lead: >-
  Rio de Janeiro, Montevideo, Santiago and Tiwanaku reveal different sides of South America: Atlantic cities, the history of capital cities and the civilisation of the high Andes. Our selection includes two itineraries, lasting 20 and 32 days. Both also pass through Argentina and Peru, so compare the complete program, time spent at attractions and order of transfers before choosing.
---

## Brazil, Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia: history on one journey

[Brazil](/brazil/), [Uruguay](/uruguay/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Bolivia](/bolivia/) are connected on two existing Ada Tours itineraries: ["Six Latin American Countries in 20 Days"](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and ["Eight South American Countries in 32 Days"](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The cultural experiences vary significantly from stop to stop.

In Brazil, travellers explore [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/); in Uruguay, the historic centre of [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/); in Chile, [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/); and in Bolivia, after travelling through the highlands, [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). Argentina and Peru lie between these stages. **Both journeys also include other countries; there is no published route restricted to these four.**

On these itineraries, history unfolds in sequence: the colonial and modern districts of large cities are followed by evidence of pre-Columbian Andean civilisation. If you want longer at specific monuments, account for flight and road-transfer days, not just the names of countries.

## Brazil: Rio as a cultural landscape

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itineraries include Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado, an excursion to Sugarloaf Mountain and time to explore the city. Mountains, the bay, beaches and historic buildings have combined to create Rio's distinctive cultural landscape. UNESCO recognised the city's cultural landscape between the mountains and the sea as a World Heritage Site.

Viewpoints reveal the city's structure from above, while walks through neighbourhoods allow visitors to compare architecture and public spaces. This is the cultural part of the Brazilian stage; [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) later in the journey are primarily a natural attraction. Both sides of the falls are visited, after which travellers continue to Buenos Aires.

Iguazu's geography needs to be understood precisely: [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) in Brazil and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) in Argentina are separate destinations on opposite sides of an international border. They complement the cultural itinerary with a major natural site, but cannot replace time in museums and historic centres.

## Uruguay: one day in Montevideo

Both programs allocate **one day for a ferry trip from Buenos Aires to Uruguay**, returning to Argentina after sightseeing in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). This is a city excursion, not a multi-day exploration of Uruguay's historical regions.

Montevideo's centre features the Old City, Independence Square, the cathedral and the port district. These are interesting to compare with the streets of Buenos Aires: the two cities grew on opposite shores of the Río de la Plata, in close historical contact, while retaining their own architecture and urban cultures.

A day provides an introduction. Studying museums, estates and other Uruguayan regions in depth would require another itinerary. Neither tour includes extra nights in Uruguay. The ferry day also needs time for embarkation and border procedures on departure from and return to Argentina.

## Chile: historic Santiago and the road toward Atacama

Travellers fly from Buenos Aires to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The city excursion includes the historic centre, Plaza de Armas, the architecture of older streets and the La Moneda Palace district. It introduces Chile's political and urban history before the route shifts to an entirely different natural environment.

Next come a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The subsequent days focus primarily on mountain roads, lagoons and crossing into Bolivia. Southern Chile and Patagonia are not part of these selected tours.

If museums and Chilean architectural heritage are the principal goal, compare other [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) with a longer urban stage. On the present itineraries, Santiago provides the main historical attractions in Chile.

## Bolivia: Tiwanaku and the civilisations of the Altiplano

After a four-wheel-drive journey past high-altitude lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the route reaches [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), where travellers depart for [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/).

Tiwanaku is one of the most significant archaeological sites of the pre-Columbian Andes. Its stone structures and ceremonial spaces tell the story of a society that existed long before the later Inca Empire. Its monuments include Kalasasaya and the Gate of the Sun. UNESCO recognises Tiwanaku as evidence of a distinctive ancient culture.

Both itineraries continue from Bolivia to Peru, including [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). These sites belong to different historical periods. Seeing Tiwanaku and Machu Picchu in sequence highlights the varied development of Andean civilisations.

## The difference between 20 and 32 days

| Tour | Cultural continuation |
|---|---|
| [20 days, 6 countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Peru, Cusco and Machu Picchu |
| [32 days, 8 countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Ecuador and Colombia as well |

Both tours cover the four selected countries plus Argentina and Peru. The 20-day journey ends in Lima. The 32-day journey continues through Ecuador and Colombia, including Quito, Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá, and schedules the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador.

Those additional 12 days **are not 12 extra days of historical excursions in Bolivia or Uruguay**. They introduce new regions and other cities. If Tiwanaku and Peruvian monuments are the priority, compare time at the attractions, excursion inclusions and overnight stays. For historic areas in Ecuador and Colombia as well, the longer journey is more suitable.

## What to consider when selecting a cultural route

Changes in elevation and climate are a major part of the journey. After the humid Brazilian regions and coastal cities, the route climbs into Atacama and the Bolivian Altiplano. Acclimatisation, how you feel at altitude and insurance covering the planned activities are especially important for travellers sensitive to elevation.

Passport and entry requirements must be checked for **every country actually visited**: Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru, plus Ecuador and Colombia on the longer tour. A one-day return trip from Argentina to Montevideo requires particular attention, as does the Chile–Bolivia land crossing. Rules depend on nationality and travel dates.

Currencies, transportation and guiding arrangements change along the route. Ada Tours helps coordinate sightseeing days with flights, road journeys and time at monuments. The exact accommodation and service inclusions should be checked in the chosen tour description.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural travel through four countries

### How much time is available in Montevideo?

One sightseeing day, including a ferry journey from Buenos Aires and a return to Argentina. Neither current tour includes several days staying in Uruguay.

### Is Tiwanaku included in both programs?

Yes. Both the [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visit Tiwanaku before continuing into Peru.

### Can I see Machu Picchu on the same journeys?

Yes. Both programs visit Peru and include [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Peru lies outside this four-country filter but remains an important part of the actual itinerary.

### Which tour offers more historic cities?

The 32-day route adds Ecuador and Colombia after Peru, including Quito, Cartagena and Bogotá. If Rio, Montevideo, Santiago, Tiwanaku and Peru's historical sites are sufficient, start by comparing the 20-day tour.

## Wine and gastronomy in Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay: the actual itinerary

This thematic selection includes the [20-day journey through six Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). The four countries in the title form part of a larger route through Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. This matters when choosing: the journey combines Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu, Montevideo, Santiago, highland Bolivia and Inca monuments, while **the wine activity is offered as an optional excursion in Chile**.

If you want a series of wine tastings in all four countries, that is not included in this program. You can, however, add a visit to Maipo Valley wineries to a rich cultural and nature journey.

## Where the gastronomic experience is actually offered

| Country | Confirmed experience |
|---|---|
| Chile | Optional tasting in Maipo |
| Uruguay | Montevideo sightseeing |
| Brazil | Rio and Iguazu, without tastings |
| Bolivia | Four-wheel-drive route and highlands |

**Chile.** On the Santiago sightseeing day, travellers may visit Maipo Valley wineries for a tasting. This optional excursion costs **230 USD per person** and requires a **minimum of 2 participants**. It is not included in the base price. A flight to Calama and transfer to San Pedro de Atacama for acclimatisation are scheduled the following day, so the winery excursion needs advance coordination.

**Uruguay.** Travellers take a day ferry trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo and return by the same route. The day includes city sightseeing and free time. No Uruguayan winery visit or paid tasting is listed. An interest in food and wine does not turn this short stop into a wine tour.

**Brazil.** The [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) days focus on Corcovado, Sugarloaf and historic districts, followed by the Brazilian side of Iguazu. The confirmed program contains no separate culinary classes or tastings.

**Bolivia.** The lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz offer natural and cultural experiences. Meals during the four-wheel-drive stage, including a packed lunch, are scheduled as part of transportation arrangements. They are not a gastronomic tour.

## Why the order of stages matters for the wine excursion

After Santiago, the route crosses Atacama toward Bolivia. The two-day four-wheel-drive stage passes high-altitude lagoons, with some sections above 4,000 metres. The program warns of possible altitude sickness and provides for an overnight stay at an expedition-style desert hotel. Adding further optional activities without time or energy reserves would be unwise.

The logical place for wine is therefore Santiago: the Maipo wineries are accessible at that stage, the optional price is known and there is a specific day in which to arrange the visit. The movement through Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia combines a ferry, flights and road transfers. These stages cannot be described as a standalone four-country gastronomic expedition: Argentina and Peru lie within the actual program.

## What is included and who this journey suits

The full tour includes 4-star hotels, domestic flights, transfers, excursions, admission tickets and meals on the specified days. International flights, optional excursions and drinks outside the program are charged separately. Choosing the Maipo wineries means an **additional 230 USD per person with at least 2 participants**, not a change in the entire itinerary's geography.

The program suits travellers who want to explore **Latin America broadly and add one wine stop in Chile**. If vineyards, local cuisine and several days of tastings are the priority, compare [food-and-wine travel](/interests/food-and-wine/) and [multi-country gastronomic journeys](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) by their actual inclusions.

All tour options covering these countries, without the thematic filter, appear in the [Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay catalogue](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_uruguay/).

## Frequently asked questions about the gastronomic stage

### Is the Maipo Valley wine tasting included in the price?

No. A visit to the wineries with tasting is offered separately for 230 USD per person, with a minimum group of 2.

### Are wineries in Uruguay and Brazil included?

No. Those stages include sightseeing in Montevideo, Rio and Iguazu. No winery visits are listed for those countries.

### Does the tour visit only these four countries?

No. The current [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) also includes Argentina and Peru. The four named countries are a thematic intersection of a longer route.

lead: >-

## Nature in Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay: how the itinerary works

The [four-country selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_uruguay/) includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a nature theme. These are the [20-day tour of six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The first also visits Argentina and Peru; the second adds Argentina, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. The catalogue combination means that all four countries are part of the main route, not that the journey goes directly through only those four.

## Brazil: Iguazu and humid forests

From Rio de Janeiro, travellers head to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side of Iguazu offers sweeping views of the waterfalls. The Argentine side occupies a separate day in both programs. The nature experience here involves humid tropical air, spray and a network of viewing trails. On the 32-day tour, the Bird Park and Macuco Safari are offered at an additional cost; the nature theme does not make them included services.

Wear shoes suitable for wet walkways and protect electronic equipment. The climate is very different from the high-altitude section in Bolivia that comes later. Compare more possibilities in [Brazil nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/).

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama before the border

After Argentina and Uruguay, travellers visit Santiago and fly to Calama before transferring to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The desert region introduces arid volcanic landscapes and is also important for altitude preparation. An evening astronomy excursion on the longer program is offered separately.

The subsequent four-wheel-drive route takes place in Bolivia. **Laguna Colorada and Uyuni should therefore not be counted as Chilean nature excursions** merely because the group departs from San Pedro. The significant difference between daytime and nighttime temperatures also needs to be considered.

## Bolivia: lagoons and the Uyuni salt flat

After the Chilean stage, travellers cross the highlands with lakes, including [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The journey then continues to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Mineral-coloured water and the extensive white salt surface are different natural sights and separate stops on the itinerary.

Long journeys in four-wheel-drive vehicles, dry air and altitude are important here. The season affects the salt flat's surface: the famous mirror effect when covered with water cannot be promised year-round. Both programs then continue to La Paz and Peru rather than heading directly to Uruguay.

## Uruguay: Montevideo is a city, not a nature park

The group reaches [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) by ferry from Buenos Aires. This is a sightseeing day in the historic centre and port. Neither tour includes a separate visit to a nature reserve in Uruguay. For a journey comparing cultures and landscapes across the continent, this stop is worthwhile; for a specialised nature trip, it adds travel logistics.

## Choosing between 20 and 32 days

| Option | Additional geography |
|---|---|
| [20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Argentina and Peru |
| [32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Argentina, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia |

The longer program adds the Galápagos Islands and Colombian cities. It appeals to travellers wanting to see island ecosystems too. If Iguazu, Atacama and Uyuni are the priorities, compare the number of days devoted specifically to them. Ada Tours can help choose a suitable pace and arrange logistics for a private option.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay

### Is there a ready-made tour covering strictly these four countries?

Both tours in the nature selection also visit other countries. A shortened itinerary would require separate route planning and pricing.

### In what order are Iguazu and Uyuni visited?

First come the waterfalls, followed by the Argentine, Uruguayan and Chilean stages, and then Bolivia and Uyuni.

### Is a Uruguayan nature reserve included?

Both tours include city sightseeing in Montevideo. A separate nature reserve in Uruguay is not scheduled.

### Where can I compare more nature destinations?

Explore the [general multi-country nature catalogue](/multi-country/interests/nature/) and [Bolivia nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/).

lead: >-
  On a journey through Brazil, Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia, visits to waterfalls and high-altitude lagoons are different from scheduled wildlife-watching activities. In this thematic selection, the 32-day tour continues to the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador, where a marine excursion to observe the islands' fauna is included. We also compare a 20-day nature itinerary without the Galápagos. Both programs feature a Montevideo city excursion in Uruguay.

## Where to watch wildlife on the journey through four countries

A journey involving [Brazil](/brazil/), [Uruguay](/uruguay/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Bolivia](/bolivia/) takes travellers from humid tropical landscapes to dry high-altitude valleys. These are very different natural environments, linked by cities and international flights.

The [32-day "Eight South American Countries" tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) is included in our "Wildlife and safari" selection because it features an island program on the Galápagos. The [20-day "Six Latin American Countries" tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) is discussed as a landscape-focused alternative; it is **not** part of this wildlife selection. Both include Argentina and Peru, so the four selected countries are only part of a broader journey. The longer trip also continues to Ecuador and Colombia. For landscape alternatives, compare the [nature selection for this same combination](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_uruguay/interests/nature/).

Distinguish **a natural attraction, an excursion involving animals and dedicated wildlife observation**. At waterfalls, the landscape may be the main attraction; at the Bird Park, visitors see birds; by high-altitude lagoons, they may observe animals in their natural habitat. But it would be wrong to call every day in every country a safari or guarantee encounters with specific species.

## Brazil: from Rio's green hills to Iguazu

The Brazilian section of both programs includes [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Excursions to Corcovado and Sugarloaf provide views of the ocean, city beaches and green hills. These are primarily sightseeing activities; a specialist wildlife-observation excursion in Rio itself is not the focus of these days.

Travellers later fly to the [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) region. The nature content becomes stronger here. Huge cascades, forest trails and viewpoints make [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) a major highlight. The Argentine side is scheduled afterwards via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

In both programs, the [Iguazu Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) and Macuco Safari boat trip are optional extras. The Bird Park offers birds in enclosures on a managed site, rather than observing them in the wild. Macuco Safari brings travellers closer to the falls by water, conditions permitting; its name does not mean a specialist animal search. These activities are not automatically included in the waterfall excursion.

For photographing birds or arranging independent walks, discuss how long to spend at each stop. Check park opening arrangements and walkway closures after bad weather, as well as restrictions affecting boat activities.

## Uruguay: a city day in Montevideo

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited by ferry from Buenos Aires on both routes, with a return to Argentina. The day focuses on its historic centre and urban attractions.

Uruguay has natural areas and an ocean coast, but **neither itinerary provides a separate marine wildlife excursion, nature reserve visit or birdwatching tour in Uruguay**. It would be wrong to add whales, sea lions or national parks to a one-day capital excursion without such activities in the confirmed program.

Uruguay is part of broader journeys combining culture and nature. A trip dedicated solely to Uruguayan wildlife would need its own route and dates.

## Chile: Atacama as the gateway to the Altiplano

After Buenos Aires, the group flies to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), then on to Calama and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This stage marks the change from low-lying humid regions to a dry desert climate.

The climb toward the Bolivian border passes through high-altitude landscapes, with open spaces, volcanic landforms and large daily temperature fluctuations. However, neither program lists a separate specialist wildlife-watching tour of Chilean Atacama. After San Pedro, the principal nature experiences belong to the subsequent four-wheel-drive journey in Bolivia.

The selected tours do not visit Chilean Patagonia, Torres del Paine or the southern penguin colonies. Those experiences require a different [Chile itinerary](/chile/tour/).

## Bolivia: salt flats and high-altitude lagoons

The strongest contrast with Brazil's nature comes in Bolivia. From Chile, the journey continues in 4×4 vehicles through the [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) region, the Salvador Dalí Desert, geothermal areas and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), then other high-altitude lagoons toward [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

These lakes are habitats for high-altitude birds, including flamingos. However, their numbers and whether they can be observed depend on the season and conditions at each stop. Watching them is a reasonable objective for a nature tour, but neither an exact number of flamingos nor a predetermined photograph can be promised.

Uyuni looks different in dry and wet seasons. Water can create a reflective surface but also restrict vehicle access to some areas. Date selection must therefore consider not just pictures of a "mirror" but actual road passability, duration of the four-wheel-drive route and access to the scheduled lagoons.

After the nature days, the itinerary continues to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), then Tiwanaku and Peru. Historical monuments here serve a different purpose and should not be confused with wildlife watching.

## Two programs: a landscape journey and island wildlife

| Tour | Principal nature experiences |
|---|---|
| [20 days, 6 countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Landscape alternative: Iguazu, Altiplano, Uyuni |
| [32 days, 8 countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Same stages plus wildlife watching on the Galápagos |

The four selected countries are covered similarly on both tours. The longer trip **does not add another 12 days in Uruguay or Bolivia**: after Peru, it reaches Ecuador, including the Galápagos Islands, then Colombia.

The [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) stage of the 32-day program includes separate island excursions, Santa Cruz's natural environment and marine areas of the archipelago. The exact stops depend on an alternative itinerary: on one day, travellers can visit North Seymour and Bachas beaches **or** South Plaza and Cape Carrión. Both alternatives must not be presented as simultaneously guaranteed.

This Ecuadorian stage makes the 32-day tour more suitable for travellers who want to combine South America's natural landscapes with dedicated island wildlife observation. However, the Galápagos are **outside the four countries in this filter** and should be compared accordingly.

## Seasons, altitude and nature safety

Rainfall, trail conditions and water levels matter at Iguazu. On the Altiplano, factors include temperature, wind, altitude, roads and water on the salt flat. There is no universal "best month" for the whole trip; dates should be chosen based on priority experiences and the complete route, not the climate of one country.

Bolivia's section is far above sea level. Altitude sickness can affect even fit travellers, so discuss health with a doctor, consider acclimatisation and verify insurance coverage. Packing must span climatic zones: light clothes for the tropics, warm wind protection for the highlands, reliable footwear and sun protection.

The programs involve international and domestic flights, border crossings and remote road stages. Ada Tours helps coordinate transfers and excursions, while actual access arrangements for parks and lagoons are confirmed for the travel dates.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife on the four-country route

### Can sightings of flamingos in Bolivia be guaranteed?

No. High-altitude lagoons are suitable bird habitats, but the presence of particular species on a particular day depends on season and natural conditions. They offer an opportunity, not a guarantee.

### Is there a safari in Uruguay on these itineraries?

No. Both programs include a one-day city excursion to Montevideo. There is no specialist nature safari in Uruguay.

### Which program includes the Galápagos?

The [32-day eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The Galápagos are in Ecuador, outside the selected four countries. The [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) ends in Peru.

### Can Uyuni and Iguazu be visited on one journey?

Yes. Both tours combine [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Argentine, Uruguayan and Chilean stages lie between them. Consider total duration and altitude, not just the distance between the two attractions.

## Bolivia, Brazil and Colombia: three countries, three different experiences

[Brazil](/brazil/) offers an Atlantic coast, large cities and waterfalls; [Bolivia](/bolivia/) offers high-altitude lagoons, [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and mountain roads; [Colombia](/colombia/) offers contrasts between [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), Caribbean [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and highland [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). The combination appeals to travellers wanting to see tropical environments, the Andes and several urban cultures on one journey. But differences in altitude, weather and air connections require a carefully planned order.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with all three countries on the **main itinerary**. That does not mean the tour is limited to Bolivia, Brazil and Colombia. The [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) runs from Brazil through Argentina, Uruguay and Chile to Bolivia, then through Peru and Ecuador to Colombia. Those other countries are full parts of the published program.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

| Country | Defining feature |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio and waterfalls |
| Bolivia | Uyuni and high altitude |
| Colombia | Andes and the Caribbean |

For a trip restricted to these three countries, we can discuss a different order of cities, flights, road transfers and duration. The price of the longer tour cannot simply be divided proportionally by the number of countries: actual costs depend on specific flights, hotels, excursions and group arrangements.

## Brazil: the ocean and Iguazu before the highlands

The published route begins in São Paulo and continues to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). City excursions include Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain. Travellers then fly to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and visit the Brazilian side of the falls, with the Argentine side scheduled for the following day. These stops differ greatly from the Bolivian lagoons to come: humid air, greenery and waterside walks rather than dry highlands.

The Iguazu region also involves international borders. [Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) lie on opposite sides. To visit both sides, check entry conditions for Argentina, border control times and current park rules. A tour mentioning the falls does not automatically guarantee visits to both countries.

On the published tour, the Bird Park and the Macuco Safari boat excursion near Iguazu are optional paid activities. When comparing tours, distinguish the included waterfall day from extra experiences. These can be arranged after confirming available time and exact service inclusions.

## Bolivia: entering through Chile, four-wheel-drive journeys and acclimatisation

**The existing itinerary does not go directly from Brazil into Bolivia.** After Argentina and Uruguay, travellers visit [Santiago de Chile](/chile/), then Calama and San Pedro de Atacama. From there they approach the Bolivian border and begin a two-day 4×4 excursion through high-altitude lagoons and geothermal areas toward [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). A flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) follows.

This is one of the most physically demanding sections. Atmospheric pressure is lower at altitude; the air is colder and drier, and even short walks can feel harder. The 32-day program includes a stop in San Pedro de Atacama for acclimatisation, but responses to altitude vary. Age and fitness alone cannot predict them. Discuss altitude-related health risks with a doctor before travelling, particularly if you have previously had symptoms of altitude sickness.

Lagoons, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and La Paz require different clothing even within Bolivia. On the four-wheel-drive section, bring warm layers, protection against wind, sun and dust, sturdy shoes, personal medication and a small supply of essentials close at hand. Roads, communications and everyday services in remote areas can differ greatly from those in Rio or Medellín.

If Bolivia is the main goal, compare this section with [Bolivia-only tours](/bolivia/tour/) and decide how important the other countries are. The Atacama crossing, salt-flat days and overnight stays must be explicit in the chosen program rather than inferred from photographs.

## Colombia: Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá have different climates even within one country

Colombia comes after Peru and Ecuador on the long itinerary. First is [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) with an excursion to Guatapé and El Peñol; then a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/); and finally [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) for city excursions and a visit to Zipaquirá. These are several different regions, not a single "Colombia day."

Climate varies significantly. Medellín lies in an Andean valley, Cartagena by the warm Caribbean Sea, and Bogotá high in the Andes, where temperatures can be noticeably cooler. So even within Colombia, a single set of clothing is insufficient. Cartagena calls for breathable lightweight fabrics and sun protection, while Bogotá requires an extra layer and protection against rain.

Within cities, consider local transfers, accommodation areas and time between airports and hotels. For sightseeing, prearranged transfers and official services are more reliable than improvised transport directly after a long flight. We help put cities and excursions into a logical sequence that accounts for travel times, although actual inclusions depend on the selected program.

Travellers interested in history can compare this stage with [Colombia's cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) and the [country overview](/colombia/) to see whether enough time is devoted to Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá.

## Why you cannot automatically assume direct flights between these three countries

Bolivia borders Brazil, and Colombia also borders Brazil. But this does not mean major tourist cities are linked by short, convenient flights. Combining [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) requires assessing real airports, connections, road stages and time to acclimatise. Available timetables depend on dates and airlines.

The published 32-day route follows a completely different order: Brazil → Argentina → Uruguay → Chile → Bolivia → Peru → Ecuador → Colombia. It includes its own compulsory stops. A journey restricted to Brazil, Bolivia and Colombia requires a new route design, not just deleting countries from the itinerary. We help compare connection options, transfer times, baggage allowances and any extra overnight stays for such a proposal.

Bolivia is particularly sensitive: the highland four-wheel-drive stage cannot be replaced by a flight if travellers want to see the lagoons and salt flat. Moving between Colombia's three major cities also requires separate transport arrangements. The more changes of airports and travel modes, the more important time buffers become.

## Passports, vaccinations and medical considerations

**Entry requirements must be checked separately for Brazil, Bolivia and Colombia** based on citizenship and passport type. The eight-country tour also requires checking every other country, including the Iguazu crossing and the border from Chile to Bolivia. Requirements can depend on previously visited countries and transit airports. Russian citizens should use consular information for each country as a starting point; other nationalities must check their own rules. There is no single visa covering the three countries.

Yellow fever is a separate consideration. Brazil, Bolivia and Colombia have different areas of epidemiological risk and requirements for proof of vaccination, depending on exact routes and countries of arrival. It would be wrong either to prescribe vaccination identically to all travellers or assume the certificate is never needed. Before departure, check current entry rules for each country, specialist travel-health guidance and individual contraindications with a doctor. The highland itinerary also warrants discussion of altitude exposure.

Check that insurance covers all countries, medical evacuation, altitude, duration and the actual planned activities. A basic policy for a beach holiday may not automatically cover a remote high-altitude 4×4 journey. Regional safety warnings, road conditions and access rules for particular areas should also be checked close to departure.

## Currencies, payments and packing for several climate zones

Brazil uses the real, Bolivia the boliviano and Colombia the Colombian peso. US dollars can be useful as a reserve or for exchange, but they are not universally accepted at every market, hotel or petrol station. Check card acceptance, fees, ATM access and cash reserves for remote areas in advance. For cards issued in Russia, confirm whether they work abroad and arrange another lawful payment method if necessary.

Packing must combine lightweight clothing for [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) with warm windproof clothes for [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). Even if the tour falls during Brazil's warmer season, high-altitude nights can be cold. Compact layers, sun and rain protection, comfortable shoes and a small separate bag for long travel days are useful. Check baggage dimensions and weights for each flight.

If your aim is to see as many contrasting regions of South America as possible in one journey, the published [32-day eight-country route](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) offers a specific sequence of cities, natural regions and transport stages. It has confirmed days, excursion formats and included services that can be examined before making an enquiry.

If your main interests are Brazil, Bolivia and Colombia, first decide which places are essential: [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) or [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). Those choices determine travel days, altitude preparation and flights. We help develop a private itinerary without presenting unconfirmed services or prices as part of an existing program.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a ready-made tour limited to Bolivia, Brazil and Colombia?

This selection features an existing journey through eight countries, including those three. A separate three-country trip can be discussed, but its route, duration and price must be calculated anew.

### Can I go directly to Uyuni after Rio?

A shorter route would require appropriate transport arrangements and an assessment of the change in altitude. On the published 32-day tour, Uyuni is reached by four-wheel-drive vehicles from Chile after other stops, not by a direct flight from Rio.

### Will I need warm clothing if the tour includes Brazil and Colombia?

Yes, if it also includes Bolivia's highlands and Bogotá. The Caribbean coast and the Altiplano require very different clothes, including protection from wind and cold.

### Is a yellow-fever vaccination certificate compulsory?

That depends on the specific countries, regions, entry points, previous travel and current rules. Check certificate requirements before flying, and discuss medical indications and contraindications with a doctor.

### Can I use one bank card in all three countries?

It cannot be guaranteed. Each country has its own currency, and card acceptance and exchange conditions depend on the bank and local restrictions. Arrange a verified payment method and a reserve.
